title: feat(scenarios): skill-evals trigger turns install the round's selection of bundles
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D4n2wzAmmp4Z6W5jsqtM2qx)_
Fixes #35858
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户无感：内部技能评测工具在「该不该加载技能」的测试里，同时装入本轮选中的全部技能包，而不是只装被测的那一个。
- 为什么做：只装一个包时「该加载」几乎全过、相邻技能抢话也看不见，技能描述改得好不好量不出来；这是重测「技能描述改动」那张卡的前提。
- 出错会怎样：只影响维护者跑评测时每轮装哪些包、怎么判分和汇总，不改任何对外发布的技能内容，可直接撤回；旧的单包方式仍可用一个参数复现。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

A `skill-evals` trigger turn (`should_trigger`) now installs the round's selection of bundles, not its own bundle alone. The selection is every bundle `--skills` names, or every bundle of the catalog when `--skills` is absent. A behaviour case keeps its own bundle alone, so its two arms still differ in exactly that bundle.

- **Design: the default, with `--trigger-field own` as the escape.** The own-bundle-only instrument is the measured defect: should-load rates sit at the ceiling and every false load is a turn reading the only skill in an empty directory. A default that keeps that number would hand it to anyone who forgets a flag, and the re-measure the card blocks needs the competing set on both legs. Comparability is kept by recording, not by the default: `round.json` records `triggerField` (`{ mode: 'selection', bundles }` or `{ mode: 'own' }`), the summary header names it, and a round recorded before reads as `own` (its header says so). `--trigger-field own` reproduces the old instrument for a like-for-like comparison with such a round.
- **Install** (`arms.ts`, `run.ts`): `installedFor(case, field)` is the one place the set is drawn (the case's own bundle first, then the field). `prepareArmWorkdir` copies each into `.claude/skills/BUNDLE/`, each without its `evals/`.
- **Grading** (`run.ts`): a should-load case still passes only when its own bundle loads; a neighbour loaded instead leaves it failed. A should-not case fails when its own bundle loads, as before. Each trigger record carries `installed` and `trigger.othersLoaded` (every other catalog bundle the turn launched or read). A with-skill turn whose init line misses an installed bundle that it should list is `invalid`, since the turn did not run the set it was meant to.
- **Summary** (`summary.ts`, `cli.ts`): the per-case trigger table gains an `other bundles loaded` column (`objectstack-ask ×12`); the header gains a `trigger turns installed ...` line.
- **Regrade**: `round.json`'s `triggerField` is carried through unchanged, and records are regraded against their own `installed`. `--trigger-field` is refused beside `--regrade` (a regrade runs no turn) and beside `--self-test`.
- **`--triggers-only` and `--skills-from`**: both work with it. Under the selection, a `--skills` bundle with no trigger case is installed as a competitor instead of being refused, as long as another named bundle has a trigger case. That is what makes the before leg runnable: published `@objectstack/skills@18.6.0` ships `objectstack-ask` with no trigger case. Alone, or under `--trigger-field own`, the bundle is still refused.
- **Self-test**: two rows (floor 32 to 34). One is a should-load case that fails because a neighbour loaded instead of its own bundle, with the neighbour named; the same row covers both bundles loaded (pass, neighbour named) and a neighbour missing from the init line (invalid). The other covers the install set in both modes, both bundles on disk without `evals/`, the flag's parse and refusals, and the caseless-competitor rule.
- **README** `skill-evals` section and an `@objectstack/scenarios` patch changeset.

Net-added lines, whole PR: +195 / -32 = 163 (budget 200).

## Tests

- `packages/qa/scenarios/test/skill-evals/skill-evals.test.ts`: one new case runs a trigger-only round through `executeRound` with a two-bundle field and a stub turn in which the neighbour takes every prompt. It asserts that both bundles are in every trigger turn's project, without `evals/`. It asserts the records: should-load `fail`, should-not `pass`, each with `installed` and `othersLoaded: ['beta-skill']`. A neighbour missing from the init line is `invalid`. `regradeRound` keeps `triggerField` in `round.json`, and the summary carries the header line and the new column. One existing expectation gains the empty column cell.
- Self-test rows above.

## Acceptance notes

- Cost per turn: the turn count and argv are unchanged. Each trigger turn's system prompt now lists 7 skill descriptions instead of 1, a small token increase per turn; no extra turn is planned.
- Without `--skills`, every catalog bundle (14 in the workspace today) is installed in every trigger turn; a bundle with no trigger case is listed in the dry run as a competitor.
- A record or `round.json` written before this change has no `installed` / `triggerField`; it regrades exactly as before, and its header reads `own bundle alone (a round recorded before --trigger-field, which always did)`.
- No model call was made. The optional real-turn check was not run: the dry run, the self-test and the vitest round all go through `prepareArmWorkdir` on disk. The earlier head-to-head streams already show Claude Code listing both bundles on the init line when both are installed.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:
1. `packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/run.ts`: `installedFor`, the init-line check on installed neighbours and `othersLoaded` in `verdictOf`, and the worker's install.
2. `packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/cases.ts`: the `competing` exception in `selectBundles`.
3. `packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/cli.ts`: how the field is drawn in `main`, the `round.json` record, and `triggerFieldLine`.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios skill-evals --skills objectstack-data,objectstack-ui,objectstack-automation,objectstack-formula,objectstack-i18n,objectstack-query,objectstack-ask --triggers-only --dry-run` prints the line below (`each trigger turn installs 7 bundle(s) ...`) and makes no model call.

All local readings at head `f6a145c065` (two feature commits plus a merge of `origin/main` at `8c18a362a2`).

<details><summary>Dry run (the card's Done-when)</summary>

```text
  objectstack-ask: 6 case(s)
  objectstack-automation: 7 case(s)
  objectstack-data: 7 case(s)
  objectstack-formula: 7 case(s)
  objectstack-i18n: 7 case(s)
  objectstack-query: 7 case(s)

each turn: a fresh directory holding the case's files; with-skill also holds .claude/skills/BUNDLE/ (no evals/)

argv (prompt on stdin): claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 16 --setting-sources project --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Skill --allowedTools Skill --mcp-config TURN_DIR/mcp.json --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence
```

The published before leg, `--skills-from 18.6.0` with the same seven bundles and `--triggers-only`, plans `42 trigger case(s) × the with-skill arm, × 1 = 42 turn(s)`, lists `objectstack-ask: no case selected; a competitor in every trigger turn` and installs the same 7 bundles. With `--trigger-field own` the same command is refused: `--skills names objectstack-ask, a bundle with no trigger case (should_trigger) under ...`.
</details>

<details><summary>Self-test</summary>

```text
  ✓ judge: a should-load case where a neighbour bundle loaded instead of its own → FAIL, the neighbour named
  ✓ arms: a trigger turn installs the round's selection beside its bundle; --trigger-field own, its bundle alone
✓ skill-evals self-test: 34 rows pass.
```
</details>

One-time ablation (not kept): `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `installedFor`'s body with the case's bundle alone (anchor 1 -> 0, marker 0 -> 1, blob 5e6484af -> 88a64de8 on disk). The new test went red: `expected [ 'load me|alpha-skill|false', ... ] to deeply equal [ ... ]` (1 failed, 37 skipped). Restored, blob equal to HEAD 5e6484af and `git diff HEAD` empty. A first attempt was a no-op that the tool refused before running anything (its replacement text already occurred in the anchor, so the marker count could not rise); it was re-run with a unique marker. The tests import `src` through vitest, not `dist`, so no rebuild leg applies.

The repo-wide lint run, `test:repo` and the type-check lanes are CI's.
